title: DistressBench: Evaluating Multi-Dimensional Crisis Support in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.12758v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language models have been adopted faster than evaluation practices that reliably assess their risks, and a growing share of use is affective rather than informational. Within that traffic users disclose suicide and self-harm (SSH) crises. Existing safety benchmarks score models primarily on refusal, but refusal is not the desired behavior here; the conversation requires a substantive supportive response. We introduce DistressBench, 718 English conversations with clinician-authored user turns spanning 23 SSH subcategories, each paired with a task-specific rubric of weighted atomic criteria across seven dimensions of crisis support and a clinician reference response. A model's score is the weighted average over the criteria its reply satisfies, reading directly as the fraction of required care delivered. The best of 25 frontier models satisfies 88.4% of weighted criteria and the median model 71.4%, against 98.7% for clinician references sc

translated_title: DistressBench：评估大语言模型的多维度危机支持能力
translated_abstract: 语言模型的普及速度超过了能够可靠评估其风险的评估实践的发展，且越来越多使用场景是情感性的而非信息性的。在这类对话中，用户会透露自杀和自残（SSH）危机。现有的安全基准主要以“拒绝回答”为模型评分，但在这种情境下拒绝并非期望的行为；对话需要的是实质性的支持性回应。我们提出了DistressBench，这是一个包含718段英文对话的基准，其用户发言由临床医生撰写，涵盖23个自杀和自残子类别，每段对话均配有针对特定任务的评分标准，即横跨危机支持七个维度的加权原子化评估指标，以及临床医生的参考回复。模型的得分是其回复所满足标准的加权平均值，可直接解读为所提供必要关怀的比例。在25个前沿模型中，表现最好的模型满足了88.4%的加权标准，中位数模型为71.4%，而临床医生参考回复达到了98.7%。
tldr: 该论文提出了DistressBench——一个包含718段由临床医生参与构建、涵盖23个自杀与自残子类别的对话基准，通过七个维度的加权评分标准评估大语言模型在危机情境下的支持能力，发现最佳前沿模型仅能提供88.4%的必要关怀，显著低于临床医生的98.7%。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces DistressBench, a benchmark of 718 clinician-authored conversations spanning 23 suicide and self-harm subcategories that evaluates multi-dimensional crisis support in LLMs, revealing that even the best frontier model delivers only 88.4% of required care compared to 98.7% for clinician references.
